predecessors.name: Anglo-Saxon England (early settlement)
predecessors.text: Cliopatria's Anglo-Saxon England shape of 523-533 contains the whole Essex shape; the page names no earlier state

successors.name: Kingdom of Wessex
successors.text: 'Sigered... in 825 ceded the kingdom to Ecgberht, King of Wessex'; the Ellendun page: 'The West Saxons succeeded in conquering Sussex, Kent, and Essex'

rulers.name: Sexred, Sæward and an unnamed brother
rulers.title: joint kings

ledger.x: 527: Æscwine founds the kingdom of the East Saxons.

c. 604: Æthelberht of Kent becomes Sæberht's overlord. He 'was in a position to exercise some authority in Essex shortly after 604'; Bede records Mellitus arriving in London in 604; the Æthelberht page calls him Sæberht's overlord and says it was he, not Sæberht, who 'built and endowed St. Pauls in London'. The…
616: Sæberht dies and Kentish overlordship lapses.
664: the East Saxon kings rule under Wulfhere of Mercia.
689: East Saxon kings are active in west Kent.
692: the East Saxon kingship in west Kent ends.

c. 750: London falls to Mercia. 'By the mid-8th century, much of the kingdom, including London, had fallen to Mercia'; the Offa page has London and Middlesex 'brought under Mercian control during Æthelbald's reign'. The year is bridged from 'mid-8th century'.
825: Mercian overlordship over Essex ends with Beornwulf's defeat at Ellendun in September 825 ('Sigered... ceded the kingdom' after the defeat of Beornwulf around 825, Essex page).
825: Sigered cedes Essex to Ecgberht of Wessex.

wars.name: Mercian suppression of the East Saxon rebellion
wars.outcome: The page: the rebellion of Sigehere and Sæbbi 'was suppressed by Wulfhere of Mercia'; the East Saxon kings were thereafter 'under Wulfhere'.

wars.name: East Saxon rule in west Kent
wars.outcome: East Saxon kings under Mercian overlordship held west Kent for a short while; Wihtred was sole king of Kent by 694.

wars.name: West Saxon conquest of the south-east (Ellendun)
wars.outcome: Ecgberht beat Beornwulf at Ellendun in September 825; Sigered ceded Essex to Ecgberht.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey line on any page opened: the Thames and Stour and the Lea are not named as frontiers; the Hertfordshire edge ('much of Hertfordshire') and west Kent are the softest.
